text: Enterprise users don’t want delight. They want to go home on time.
receipt: Seven years designing enterprise IT software. Brutal UX zeroes every transition so state changes land in the same frame.

text: A design system is a mood board until a script can fail it.
description: linefield’s build refuses to run when its manifest, pieces and README disagree, and its control audit fails any control that changes nothing.
receipt: linefield’s build refuses to run when the manifest, the pieces and the README disagree, and its control audit fails anything that reads a value without changing a pixel.

text: AI gets you to 80% by lunch. The last 20% is still the job.
receipt: My essay *The Last 20%* is about exactly where AI prototyping stops saving time.

text: An accessibility report nobody can find is a liability with a cover page.
receipt: VPAT Vault exists so evidence moves into the report instead of ending up in a separate silo.

text: Decoration is where hierarchy goes to hide.
receipt: Brutal UX strips every radius, shadow and easing at once. The hierarchy survives. It moves from the channel you scan to the one you read.

text: Software should be disposable. Your data shouldn’t be.
receipt: *The Disposable Architecture of Tomorrow*, plus a second brain kept in plain Markdown so the knowledge walks with me when the tools don’t.

text: Dead controls do more damage than dark patterns, because nobody goes looking for them.
description: Twice, a linefield control shipped that read its value and changed nothing, and a human review passed it both times.
receipt: Twice, a linefield control shipped that read its value and changed nothing, and a human review passed it both times. My old portfolio had one too: a menu button that did nothing above 768 px.

text: A design review that can’t cite a number is an opinion with a calendar invite.
description: UX Skill Repo ties every finding to a contrast ratio or a named law, so “improve the hierarchy” becomes a rule ID and a fix.
receipt: UX Skill Repo ties every finding to a contrast ratio or a named law, so “improve the hierarchy” becomes a rule ID and a fix. Terry Time wrote down how its storefront test gets decided before the first visitor arrived.

text: Background automation without a status page is a haunting.
receipt: The Agent Bench checks its own health every four hours and says what broke before I notice. Agentic Light goes further: nothing runs that I didn’t start.

text: Build the extreme version first. Then buy back only the comfort you can justify.
receipt: Brutal UX is my control group. Once everything is gone, every radius and shadow added back has to earn its place.

text: Hiring managers don’t read case studies. They read captions and numbers.
receipt: So every case study opens with a title block, and every lead screenshot gets numbered callouts.

text: Breaking things is a design method. You don’t grow out of it.
receipt: *Built to Break*: how a childhood urge to destroy things built a career in multimodal design.
